chunks: 2308 - Zurārah ibn Aʿyan said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: “Did you meet al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام?” He said:

“Yes. I remember while I was with him in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām, and the flood had entered it, and the people were fearing for the Maqām. One going out would say, ‘The flood has carried it away,’ and one entering would say, ‘It is in its place.’”

He said: “So he said, ‘O so-and-so, what are these people doing?’ I said, ‘May Allah set your affairs aright, they fear that the flood may have carried away the Maqām.’ He said, ‘Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made it a sign; it would not be taken away by it, so be at ease.’”
And the place of the Maqām, which Ibrāhīm عليه السلام had placed, was at the wall of the House. It remained there until the people of al-Jāhiliyyah moved it to the place where it is today.
Then when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم conquered Makkah, he returned it to the place where Ibrāhīm عليه السلام had placed it, and it remained there until ʿUmar came to authority.

So he asked the people, ‘Which of you knows the place where the Maqām had been?’ A man said to him, ‘I had taken its measure with a strap, and it is with me.’ He said, ‘Bring it to me.’ So he brought it to him, and he measured it, then returned it to that place.

key_terms.السَّيْلُ: the floodwater that entered the sanctuary
key_terms.الْمَقَامِ: Maqām Ibrāhīm, the station associated with Prophet Ibrāhīm عليه السلام
key_terms.عَلَمًا: a sign or landmark appointed by Allah
key_terms.مِقْدَارَهُ: its measured position or exact measure

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the history and original location of Maqām Ibrāhīm?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a memory of Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām during a flood, when he reassured people that Allah had made the Maqām a sign and it would not be lost. It also narrates the history of the placement of Maqām Ibrāhīm, from its original position set by Ibrāhīm عليه السلام, its relocation by the people of al-Jāhiliyyah, its restoration by the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and its later repositioning in the time of ʿUmar.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2308 - Zurara ibn A'yan said to Abu Ja'far (as): "Did you meet Imam Al-Husayn (as)?"
Imam (as) replied: "Yes, I remember being with him in the Sacred Mosque when a flood entered it, and the people were worried about the Maqam (Station of Ibrahim). Someone would go out and say: 'The flood has taken it away,' and another would come in and say, 'It is still in its place.'
Imam Al-Husayn (as) said: 'O so-and-so, what are these people doing?'
I said: 'May Allah (swt) rectify your affairs, they fear that the flood might have taken the Maqam.' He said: 'Indeed, Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, has made it a sign; it will not be taken away. Be at ease.'
The Maqam was originally placed by Ibrahim (as) next to the wall of the Kaaba, and it remained there until the people of Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance) moved it to its current location. 
When the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him and his family) conquered Mecca, he returned it to the spot where Ibrahim (as) had placed it, and it stayed there until the caliphate of Umar.
Umar asked the people: 'Who among you knows the original location of the Maqam?'
A man said: 'I know. I had measured its position with a strap, and I still have it.'
Umar said: 'Bring it to me.'
The man brought it, and Umar measured the position and returned the Maqam to that location."
